spans.text: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants, “bhikkhavo”ti.

entries.task_id: who assert|a|self that is neither percipient nor non-percipient and healthy after death
entries.description: who assert a self that is neither percipient nor non-percipient and healthy after death
entries.subject: who assert
entries.object: self that is neither percipient nor non-percipient and healthy after death

spans.text: There are ascetics and brahmins who assert a self that is neither percipient nor non-percipient and healthy after death, describing it as formed, or formless, or both formed and formless, or neither formed nor formless.

Now, the ascetics and brahmins who assert the annihilation, eradication, and nonexistence of an existing being reject those who assert a self that is healthy after death, whether percipient or non-percipient or neither percipient nor non-percipient.

spans.text: Seyyathāpi nāma vāṇijassa vāṇijjāya gacchato evaṁ hoti: Suppose a trader was going to market, thinking: iti viditvā tassa nissaraṇadassāvī tathāgato tadupātivatto.
